1.explanation: The replacement logic in ReplaceConnectionBehavior (in both fixConnection and replaceReconnectedConnection) creates a new sequence flow but never updates its semantic or DI parent to the target participant. The BPMN updater’s methods (updateSemanticParent and updateDiParent) are responsible for moving elements between containers in the BPMN XML and DI model. Because these hooks aren’t invoked after replacement, the new flow remains tied to the old parent, leading to incorrect rendering and modeler instability.
1.bug_scenario: When you replace a message flow from Participant A to Participant B with a sequence flow, the newly created sequence flow remains inside the original participant (A) instead of moving into the target participant (B). Visually, after reconnecting the dotted message‐flow arrow into a loop, you expect the replacement sequence flow to live (and render) inside Participant B’s swimlane, but it remains in Participant A’s container (red highlight), and in some cases the modeler even crashes.

2.explanation:
• ReplaceConnectionBehavior.fixConnection: this function creates a new connection when swapping MessageFlow <> SequenceFlow but never updates the new sequence flow’s parent to the target Participant’s process.  
• ReplaceConnectionBehavior.replaceReconnectedConnection: on reconnection it builds and wires a replacement connection but again omits assigning the proper semantic/DI parent.  
• BpmnUpdater.prototype.updateParent: responsible for rehoming BPMN elements (including connections) when their containing process or collaboration changes. Its current stub doesn’t handle connections being moved across Pools/Processes after replacement.  
• BpmnUpdater.prototype.updateConnection: meant to update the BPMN XML and DI relationship of a reconnected edge. Without implementing parent reassignment here, a new sequence flow remains in the wrong container.  

Together these routines are where the missing parent‐reassignment logic for newly created sequence flows must be added to ensure the element is owned by the correct Participant’s Process and rendered properly.
2.bug_scenario: When you replace a message flow between two Participants (A → B) with a sequence flow, the newly created sequence flow is never moved into the target Participant’s Process container. Visually it remains attached to the original pool (or no pool), so it’s not rendered in B’s lane and may crash the modeler.
